bottleneck: Brain tumors sit behind the blood-brain barrier, which excludes most chemotherapeutics and antibodies while the tumor itself disrupts the barrier unevenly — creating unpredictable drug exposure where some regions get toxic doses and others get none. Convection-enhanced delivery is invasive and distributes poorly, focused ultrasound opening is transient and hard to repeat, and systemic dose escalation poisons the body before reaching the tumor. Effective systemic therapy for brain tumors awaits a delivery science that does not yet exist, and drug discovery is pointless without it: the best molecule in the world fails if it cannot reach its target.
current_state: BBB-opening trials show increased drug delivery on imaging, but no approach has translated into survival gains for brain tumor patients.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Health: From Code to Cure

title: Brain tumor drugs blocked by uneven BBB
why_it_blocks: Oncology's best weapons cannot reach brain tumors reliably. Delivery, not drug discovery, is the binding constraint on neuro-oncology — and it receives a fraction of the funding.
